note: Bundled Claude Code skills this skill competes with for retrieval. Proves the description STAKES a boundary where an overlap exists; it does NOT prove the model honours it, which only tests/routing-live measures.
coverageNote: 5 of 12 bundled skills recovered. The rest sit in minified variable assignments with their descriptions decoupled, or extracted a value that could not be verified. Listed rather than hidden.

bundled.schedule: Create and manage scheduled remote Claude Code agents
bundled.security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch
bundled.update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
bundled.keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
bundled.fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.

overlaps.why: Scheduled remote agents are an operating surface. This library covers declaring workers, not scheduling them.

Its description claims "hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files", and it won retrieval on benchmark question GQ-06 ("claude code stop hook not working"), which then scored 1 of 6 because the workspace was audited instead of the mechanism contract being answered. The split we claim: EDITING configuration is update-config; explaining why a documented mechanism does not fire, with no artifact attached, is this skill.

It generates an allowlist from observed transcripts, which is a data-driven settings edit. This library explains what a permission rule is consulted for and where enforcement leaks. A user asking to reduce prompting wants the former.
